name: Dark Aqua
lede: Dark Aqua is a deep, muted blue-green closer in our data to [[petrol|Petrol]] than to its own parent color, [[aqua]].

sections.title: A modifier that lands on a different name
sections.body:
The name is ordinary grammar, "dark" plus [[aqua]], recorded by the 2010 xkcd color survey and otherwise undocumented in the older dictionaries and standards our library draws on [1]. No CSS, Wikipedia, Ridgway, or ISCC-NBS entry shares this exact value [1].

Measured in our library, its closest learnable match is [[petrol|Petrol]], about 5.5 CIEDE2000 units away, nearer than its own base name [[aqua]] [1]. Siblings in the same muted blue-green range are [[aqua]], [[petrol|Petrol]], [[teal]], and [[dark-slate-grey|Dark Slate Grey]] [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this deep blue-green in just 13 of 23,781 paintings, as photographed, about 0.05 percent, one of the rarest matches in this color's part of the archive [2]. The earliest and largest match is Raphael's *The Niccolini-Cowper Madonna* (1508); the only painter with more than one hit is unrecorded, so no painter stands out at a meaningful count [2]. Switzerland's paintings carry it over fourteen times the archive average, though on a very small base [2].
